_comment: Recorded baseline for the AgentFuse eval. CI asserts we never fall below these. A floor, not an achievement. The generated suite (536 scenarios) is the statistically meaningful one; the 16 hand-written cases are named regression cases. Recovery metrics added 2026-08-12 - before that, AgentFuse's central claim ('it steers the agent back') was completely unmeasured.
config_note: drift_threshold default lowered 0.45 -> 0.20 on 2026-08-12 based on the threshold sweep: F1 66.0->73.3, FPR 39.0->10.8, premature trips 54->0, at a cost of 6.4 points of recall. | LoopDetector rewritten 2026-08-12 to require an identical RESULT, not just an identical call: FPR 11.8%->4.9%, precision 82.5%->92.0%, F1 72.2%->75.7%, recall unchanged. Call-only fallback at 2x threshold still catches loops whose output varies cosmetically. | NoProgressDetector rewritten 2026-08-12: the old one incremented its stall counter ONLY on a repeated state hash, but a genuine stall emits no state updates at all, so the trip condition was unreachable - it required evidence of state changes to detect their absence. Now counts weighted actions since the last genuine advance. recall 64.3->89.2, F1 75.7->91.5, progress family 0%->100%, FPR unchanged at 4.9%. | LoopDetector args normalised (case/whitespace/punctuation) 2026-08-12: loop recall 65.5->100 on cosmetic variants, attribution restored 86.9->99.1. Then a REWORDED-args generator was added to keep the benchmark honest, which correctly pulled loop recall back to 89.5% and overall to 87.9%. | BENCHMARK FIDELITY FIX 2026-08-12: the eval was emitting an event stream production never produces (tool_call without the preceding llm_call, tokens on the tool call, standalone STATE_UPDATE events). Corrected against a captured openai-agents trace. recall 87.9->92.4, F1 90.9->93.4, detection ~0.5 steps faster. Also exposed a real production bug: LoopDetector only reset on event.type==STATE_UPDATE, but the AgentKit adapter attaches state to TOOL_RESULT, so in production it never reset on genuine progress. | PHASE 2 (verified + memoried recovery) 2026-08-12: steering was single-shot - inject and never check. Added a verification step (did state advance within verify_window?) and a memory of (failure signature -> steer -> worked?), so a failed rung is ruled out and the engine climbs a ladder of genuinely different interventions (re-anchor -> alternate-action -> challenge-assumption -> decompose -> escalate) instead of rephrasing. recovery rate 87.6->95.0, steering usable 87.6->100. | max_recoveries 3 -> 5: the ladder has 4 steerable rungs, so a cap of 3 made its upper rungs unreachable dead code. Measured 55.4 -> 75.2 recovery rate; plateaus above 5. | ADAPTIVE CALIBRATION 2026-08-12: per-run baselines learned ONLY from stretches evidenced healthy (a state advance), widening thresholds and never tightening them. Measured A/B on the full suite: FPR 15.0 -> 8.6%, precision 84.7 -> 90.6%, F1 88.7 -> 91.8%, recall unchanged at 93.1%. Showed NO benefit on the old short-scenario suite, which is what prompted adding long runs.

known_weak_families.drift: 90% with LOCAL embeddings (bge-base-en-v1.5, 110M params, free, offline), up from 76% on the lexical fallback. Model size has a hard floor here: bge-small (33M) is not merely weaker, it ranks gradual drift as MORE similar to the goal than genuinely on-task text, so any threshold built on it fires backwards.
known_weak_families.attribution: 84% - reworded-argument loops are caught by PROGRESS as a backstop rather than by LOOP, so the steering advice is blunter than ideal. Needs semantic argument comparison to fix properly.
known_weak_families.roi: 1.70x, down from 3.85x - the closed-loop measurement charges every steering attempt, and climbing a ladder costs more calls than giving up after one. The old figure only ever charged for a single attempt.
known_weak_families.long_sparse: 42.5% FPR on workloads with wide gaps between state advances, down from 100% with calibration off. Not solved - the first cycle still trips before any baseline exists. Now the single largest FP source: 17 of the 39 remaining false positives, all fired by LOOP.
known_weak_families.progress: 100%, up from 67%. Both gaps closed: gen_oscillate by the rewritten stall detector, gen_zeno by the new RateOfProgressDetector.
known_weak_families.loop_detector_verdict_RESOLVED: Was at ablate-loop dF1 +1.8 (removing it IMPROVED the system). Now dF1 +0.0 with 0 false positives, after three fixes: (a) error-shaped results get 2x patience, since an identical HTTP 503 is a healthy retry rather than an agent re-asking a question it already answered - FP 22 -> 6; (b) the call-only fallback now judges on the RESULT, not the call; (c) 14 of its FPs were a benchmark artifact, not a detector defect. KEEP DECISION, now evidence-based: removing it holds recall at exactly 97.6% (it detects nothing unique) but drops attribution 84.1% -> 56.2%, because it is the only detector that names the offending TOOL. 'Stop calling search_files' is actionable; 'you seem stuck' is not. The product claim is steering, not detection, so 28 points of attribution is worth more than the 0.0 F1 it now costs.
known_weak_families.OUTCOME_BEFORE_VERDICT_RULE: A supervisor must not act on an action whose outcome it has not yet seen. A tool step emits llm_call -> tool_call -> tool_result; a detector that tests its threshold on the CALL can halt a run one event before the result that would have cleared it. This shipped in TWO detectors independently (loop, then progress) and a test found a THIRD instance (loop's call-only fallback). Each time the runs killed were ones about to succeed - the worst possible failure mode for a guardrail. Now asserted for all stateful detectors in evals/test_rate.py. Cost of the progress instance alone: 16 false positives, FPR 7.4% -> 4.1% when fixed.
known_weak_families.domain_pack_entropy: REALISM WEAKNESS, unfixed. Each domain offers 4 tools and exactly 4 distinct argument dicts. Any generator that draws 'varied work' at random therefore produces identical (tool, args, result) triples by accident - measured at 199/200 runs for gen_long_sparse_benign, worst case 11 identical calls labelled healthy. That one was fixed; the OTHER generators have not been audited for the same accidental repetition, and the low entropy also makes every scenario less representative of real agent traces than it appears.
known_weak_families.zeno_bare_cursor: The rate detector needs TWO quantities - one pinned, one climbing past it. A Zeno trap that reports only a bare cursor ('batch 7 done') is NOT detectable and will be missed, because that is character-for-character what a healthy batch job emits. Measured cost of ignoring this: the first version fired on any unbounded rising counter and produced 44 FPs on healthy runs (FPR 8.9 -> 17.0). The narrower claim is the one the evidence supports.

generated_suite.recovery_note: recovery_rate DROPPED 95.0 -> 75.2 on 2026-08-12 because the old number was CIRCULAR, not because the system got worse. It unlocked the recovery branch whenever our own rubric approved our own instruction - but the rubric and the ladder's templates were written together, so it always approved them, and every rung unlocked the same branch (making the ladder's value unmeasurable). Scenarios now declare responds_to: the single rung that agent actually obeys, ground truth independent of anything we generate. 75.2% is the first recovery number that could have come out wrong. steering_usable=100% remains circular by construction and should NOT be read as evidence. Fell again 75.2 -> 71.7 when three harder positive families were added; the suite got harder, the system did not regress.
generated_suite.suite_note: Three LONG-RUN generators added 2026-08-12 (gen_long_then_loop, gen_long_polling_benign, gen_long_sparse_benign). The suite had a median length of 7 steps, which is a poor proxy for 'hours of autonomous execution' and made adaptive calibration untestable - only 39% of scenarios ever accumulated enough healthy samples for it to engage. The floors here are lower than the pre-2026-08-12 numbers because the SUITE GOT HARDER, not because the system regressed: FPR 5.2% was measured before long sparse-progress workloads were represented at all.
generated_suite.rate_detector_note: RATE-OF-PROGRESS DETECTOR added 2026-08-13, closing the last documented known gap. The binary progress test asks 'did the state advance?', so an agent that advances on EVERY step and converges on none resets the stall counter every step and its trip condition is unreachable - no value of stall_patience reaches it. Measured on the full suite: recall 88.4 -> 97.6, F1 89.6 -> 94.6, FPR 8.9 -> 8.0, progress family 67 -> 100%. Ablation puts its causal contribution at dF1 -4.8, third largest of five detectors. Two findings came out of building it. (1) The first version tripped on any unbounded rising counter and cost 44 false positives on healthy runs (FPR 8.9 -> 17.0) - 'batch 7 done' is the same evidence as 'processed 1 of many (offset 7)', so a lone climbing counter is NOT identifiable and the detector now abstains on it. (2) Attribution fell 84 -> 69.8 in that same version because gen_bloat (a spend scenario) matched the loose signature; requiring the two-quantity signature fixed both at once, which is what a shared root cause looks like. Spend family recall fell 100 -> 96.3 (3 FNs) because the rate detector is no longer covering for the spend detector on gen_bloat - a pre-existing spend weakness that was previously hidden, not a new regression.
generated_suite.SUITE_IS_SATURATED_2026_08_13: ⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT ENTRY IN THIS FILE. The system now scores F1 98.1%, FPR 1.2%, 6 false positives out of 487 hard negatives. A benchmark you score 98% on has stopped being a measuring instrument - it can no longer tell a good change from a neutral one, and every remaining signal is 6 FPs and 11 FNs wide. Three specific reasons NOT to read these numbers as 'nearly production ready': (1) the generators encode MY model of agent failure, so this measures self-consistency, not real-world coverage; (2) part of today's gain came from FIXING A GENERATOR - a legitimate correction with evidence, but making the test easier is exactly how benchmarks stop meaning anything, and it must stay visible; (3) the ceiling effect below now dominates the intervals. The correct next move is HARDER AND MORE REALISTIC SCENARIOS, especially from captured real traces, not further tuning against this suite. Any future gain measured only here should be treated as unproven.
generated_suite.clustering_ceiling_effect_warning: DO NOT quote the effective sample size from the 2026-08-13 run as evidence of a better-powered benchmark. Design effect fell 16.9x -> 2.02x and ICC 0.407 -> 0.048, moving effective n from 13 to 222 and narrowing the clustered recall interval from [57.8-95.7] to [94.8-99.0]. That is a CEILING ARTIFACT: 18 of 20 recall clusters are now all-successes, so between-cluster variance has nowhere to live and DEFF collapses toward 1 by construction. The suite did not gain independent evidence - it went from 20 generator families to 21. The number of independent families remains the only real measure of statistical power, and the interval will widen again the moment any family regresses. recall_clustered_low is deliberately floored at 0.70 rather than near the measured 0.948 for exactly this reason: a small regression will re-inflate ICC and blow through a tight floor for statistical rather than behavioural reasons.
generated_suite.tier1_confidence_note: PHASE 4 TIER 1 (token logprobs), measured 2026-08-13 and NOT SHIPPED ON. The signal is real: against Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-Q4, n=14 generations per condition, healthy reasoning averaged -0.686 mean logprob (sd 0.068) while all three failure conditions separated beyond their 95% CIs - stuck_loop -0.775 (d=0.87), offtopic -0.830 (d=1.44), trap -0.842 (d=1.68) - and critically the AMBIGUOUS-BUT-HEALTHY control did NOT drop (-0.707, d=0.28), so the signal tracks failure rather than difficulty. AND YET THE DETECTOR IS HARMFUL. Ablation on the full suite: dF1 +10.8 for REMOVING it. Recall identical at 97.6% (it caught nothing the behavioural detectors missed), precision 98.6 -> 78.9, FPR 1.2% -> 26.7%, 118 extra false positives, attribution 83.8 -> 68.3. THE LESSON, which generalises: a large effect size in a controlled comparison does NOT make a usable per-event detector. Cohen's d of 1.4 still means heavy per-turn overlap, and across a long run with many turns even a 3-consecutive-turn requirement fires constantly on healthy work. Base rate and run length dominate effect size. Kept as opt-in (cfg confidence=True) with the measurement recorded, because the module is useful to someone whose agent emits logprobs and who wants the raw signal - but shipping it enabled would have cost 10.8 F1 for zero detections.

handwritten_suite.note: All 16 hand-written cases now pass. The four entries formerly listed as known misses (drift_gradual_slide, drift_abrupt_hijack, loop_semantic_variants, stall_busy_no_progress) were resolved by the detector work on 2026-08-12. Held at a perfect floor deliberately: these are NAMED regression cases, so any future failure here is a regression, not a tuning trade-off.

significance.note: F1 must significantly exceed a rate-matched random control (p < 0.05).

economics_note: 'tokens saved' is WASTE AVOIDED (what the doomed run would have burned after the halt), not net benefit including completing the task. The recovered path's own cost is charged to tokens_spent. Treat ROI as an upper bound on the real economic case.
statistical_note: Scenarios from one generator share a template and behave near-identically, so they are NOT independent samples. Nominal Wilson intervals therefore overstate precision. The report now shows cluster-adjusted intervals (Kish design effect, DEFF = 1 + (m-1)*ICC) and those are the ones to quote. Practical consequence: adding scenarios PER GENERATOR buys no statistical power at all - only adding more independent generators does. Measured on the generated suite: ICC 0.407, design effect 16.9x, effective n=19 against a nominal 320. Nominal recall CI [89.8-95.4]; HONEST CI [75.4-99.1]. The clustered lower bound is the number to defend, and it is floored at 0.70 rather than the nominal 0.90 because that is what the evidence actually supports. MEASURED CORRECTION to earlier advice: effective sample size tracks the NUMBER OF GENERATORS, not the scenario count. Sweeping scenarios-per-generator across 40/20/10/5 (total 880/440/220/110) moved effective n only 13->14 and left the honest interval essentially unchanged. Running 40 per generator therefore costs 8x the compute of 5 for zero additional evidence. n_per_generator buys DIAGNOSTIC resolution (stable per-family rates for finding bugs), not statistical power. The single lever on the interval is more independent generator families.
embedding_note: Drift detection was blocked on OpenAI credits for most of this work. It is not any more: a local 110M ONNX model resolves it for free, offline, at ~4ms per sentence on CPU - faster than a network call and with no third party seeing the agent's reasoning. Measured separation of the case that matters (gradual drift, where the agent keeps the goal's vocabulary while its intent slides): lexical ~0.05 overlapping window; bge-small INVERTED (drift 0.756 > on-task 0.712); bge-base separable with gap +0.043. Threshold 0.65 chosen by sweep: 0.60 gives drift recall 83%, 0.65 gives 97% at FPR 6%, 0.69 gives 100% but FPR 11.5%.
